scenes.text: If a cheap model writes the code and an expensive one checks it, who checks the checker?
scenes.say: If a cheap model writes the code, and an expensive model checks it, who checks the checker?

scenes.headline: How shadcn's improve splits coding between two models
scenes.sub: A skill that writes plans, hands them off, and reviews the diff
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ulric! Today it's improve, a skill by Shad C N that splits coding between a strong model and a cheap one. Let's read what it actually does.

scenes.title: The plan is the product
scenes.sub: Four markdown files, and no code at all
scenes.say: Chapter one. The plan is the product.

steps.term: Advisor: the strong model that only plans
steps.say: The advisor is whatever strong model your session runs. It reads the repo, and it is never allowed to edit source code.
It audits, vets every finding against the code itself, and writes one plan per finding you pick, into a plans folder.

steps.term: Worktree: a separate checkout of the same repo
steps.say: With execute, a cheaper subagent gets the whole plan pasted into its prompt and edits a disposable git worktree.
Then the advisor reviews the result. And merging? That always stays with you.
Here is everything in it. The skill file sets the role: a senior advisor, not an implementer.
Three references: how to audit, how to write a plan for the weakest plausible executor, and how to close the loop.
One real example plan, and a Claude Code plugin manifest. There is no program anywhere. The product is instructions.

scenes.title: What the check really is
scenes.sub: Not a separate verifier: the advisor again
scenes.say: Chapter two. What the check really is.

scenes.text: The cheap model types the plan; the same strong model that wrote the plan re-runs its checks and grades the diff.
scenes.say: Here's the idea. The cheap model types the plan. Then the same strong model that wrote it re-runs its checks and grades the diff.

steps.say: The plan inlines everything: why it matters, excerpts of the current code, steps that each end in a command, and stop conditions.

steps.term: Drift check: did the planned files change?
steps.say: The executor checks for drift first, then edits, runs the tests, and reports. Here it also touched a file the plan never listed.
The advisor re-runs every done criterion itself, then diffs the worktree against the plan's file list. Out of scope fails, full stop. Revise.
Round two. The executor fixes it, every gate passes, and the verdict is approve. The skill allows at most two revision rounds.
Even approved, nothing is merged. You get a branch and a summary.

scenes.title: What each stage costs the strong model

steps.say: The repo's example plan runs to one thousand one hundred and forty-nine words. A plan is a document the strong model pays for.
Execution is the long loop of edits, test runs and re-reads. This is the only part moved to the cheap model.
The review reads the plan, the diff and the test logs again, at the strong model's price.
Every revision round repeats some execution and a whole review.

scenes.title: Does it save money?
scenes.sub: List prices, and token counts I chose
scenes.say: Chapter three. Does it save money?

scenes.label: Opus 5.5 over Sonnet 5.5, per token, on list prices
scenes.note: the skill's default executor is sonnet
scenes.say: On this site's list prices, Opus five point five costs only twice what Sonnet five point five does per token. And Sonnet is the default executor.

scenes.title: A refactor, priced
scenes.say: On a refactor I sized myself, the Sonnet split saves twenty-seven percent on a clean pass. One revision round, and it costs more than Opus alone. With Haiku, the saving survives.

scenes.title: Where the loop is blind
scenes.say: Some faults get past every gate.

items.text: Drift check sees listed files only
items.say: The drift check only diffs the files a plan names. Change a caller it never listed, and nothing notices.

items.text: Planner and reviewer are one model
items.say: The plan, its done criteria and the review all come from one model. If it misread the code, all three agree with the mistake.
And only a careful read catches a test written to pass.

scenes.text: The split pays when execution dwarfs the plan and the review. Pick a cheap executor that is really cheap.
scenes.say: The split pays when execution dwarfs the plan and the review. So pick plans with long, mechanical execution, and an executor that is really cheap.

recap: The check is the advisor again
scenes.say: To recap. The advisor plans and never edits. The check is the advisor again. And the default executor is only half price.
